lens: Recruitment operator — ambiguous result (simulated expertise/user lens)
reason: The operator workflow has substantial safeguards: explicit irreversible-close language, separate submitted/valid coverage, reviewed release cohorts, per-applicant blockers and dossier links. The supplied desktop and mobile modal captures show clear hierarchy and restrained Precision Instrument styling. The public proposition clearly explains student-led consulting; the Join preparation-to-evaluation journey is supported by source and recorded synthetic browser checks. Resume copy accurately discloses original-PDF access, and unpublished case studies remain explicitly pending approval. However, ambiguous grading-close acknowledgements leave misleading recovery choices, and cohort coverage can call partial evidence Complete. These concrete operator gaps prevent world-class agreement. This is independent source/capture/log assessment, not observed operator success or hosted acceptance.

findings.evidence: useRushAction reports Request failed on a rejected POST and refreshes only on success. RoundStatusControl.saveStatus (round-status-control.tsx:60-66) leaves its ready confirmation open when act returns false. If freezing commits before the acknowledgement is lost, the dialog still offers Keep grading open and another close. operator-close.spec.ts:85 tests coverage-GET failure, not this committed-write ambiguity.
findings.userImpact: An operator cannot tell whether grading remains open after an irreversible action; the cancellation label can imply a state that no longer exists. The SQL same-status no-op makes retry safe, but does not correct the stale explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: On uncertain close acknowledgement, report an unknown result, reconcile current round status, and replace stale choices with confirmed closed state or explicit reload/retry guidance. Add a commit-then-response-loss test.

findings.evidence: The cohort status renders Complete for SUBMITTED coverage. group-case-coverage.ts derives that state solely from assignment statuses. round_close_summary.sql tests explicitly establish that two submitted Group Case observations can yield zero valid evaluations when minimum observation requirements are unmet.
findings.userImpact: An operator scanning cohort coverage can mistake saved partial evidence for finished grading, although the separate results and closing summary correctly distinguish validity.
findings.suggestedFix: Label this state All assignments submitted, or derive Complete from canonical valid independent coverage. Cover the two-submitted-but-invalid case in the board presentation.

notVerified: No staging, hosted Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration, deployment or migration rollout was exercised; local SQL logs report 709 passing assertions and the focused browser log reports 18 passing synthetic checks.
No actual operator completed cohort management, closing, outcome release or recovery in an authenticated session. No human usability study exists.
The supplied operator captures show a synthetic modal, not live cohort/results/release screens. Mobile scroll completion, assistive technology, physical devices, Safari and Firefox remain unverified.
Board approval of resume policy, client publication approvals and actual project artifacts remain external dependencies.
